cd09f9fc8c7d6a25.en: <1>Microsoft Store apps (Microsoft Store / UWP / MSIX): </1>Typically located at <2>C:\Program Files\WindowsApps</2>, managed by the AppX deployment service, package signing, ACL permissions, and store update mechanisms. Forcing migration via directory junctions can cause apps to fail to start, store update failures, or permission damage. Therefore, Viap does not treat these as migratable apps. Some store apps can be moved via the "Move" button in Windows Settings, or by adjusting the default save location for new apps in Storage settings. These system capabilities should be prioritized.

d3fd58fdf8debdce.en: <1>App Management (App Migration):</1> Scan installed apps on the system and migrate their installation directories to another disk. For regular desktop apps, migration typically allows normal startup, updates, and uninstallation. It is suitable for moving large apps (such as IDEs, games) out of the system drive when C drive space is insufficient. Microsoft Store apps are maintained by Windows' package management system and are not recommended for migration via directory junctions; some apps provide a 'Move' button in Windows Settings, and you can also adjust the default save location for new apps via Storage Settings. It is recommended to prioritize Windows-provided migration methods.
